source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Ruth 1–4: all 85 public verses bind one-to-one to the matching original Hebrew records. Later chapters are outside this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Sets the judges-era frame and temporary residence before the family moves.
verses.before: In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live for a time in the country of Moab, along with his wife and two sons.
verses.after: In the days when the judges governed, a famine struck the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live for a time in the country of Moab, taking his wife and two sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land, and a man of Bethlehem in Judah went to dwell in the fields of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.

verses.rationale: Separates names, origin and arrival without losing Ephrathite identity.
verses.before: The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi, and his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to the country of Moab and remained there.
verses.after: The man was named Elimelech, his wife Naomi, and his two sons Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to Moab and stayed there.
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the names of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion; they were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came into the fields of Moab and remained there.

verses.rationale: Keeps Naomi at the center of the first bereavement.
verses.before: Then Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
verses.after: Then Naomi’s husband Elimelech died, leaving her with her two sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Elimelech, the husband of Naomi, died, and she was left, she and her two sons.

verses.rationale: Retains approximate duration and the women’s Moabite identity.
verses.before: They married Moabite women. One was named Orpah, and the other Ruth. They lived there about ten years.
verses.after: Her sons married Moabite women, one named Orpah and the other Ruth. They lived there for about ten years.
verses.tsw_comparator: These took Moabite wives; the name of the one was Orpah and the name of the other Ruth. And they lived there about ten years.

verses.rationale: Preserves the narrator’s repeated loss and designation of sons as children.
verses.before: Then both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left without her two sons and her husband.
verses.after: Then both Mahlon and Chilion died too. The woman was left without her two children and without her husband.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then both Mahlon and Chilion also died, so that the woman was left without her two sons and her husband.

verses.rationale: Makes the reason for returning audible while preserving divine attention.
verses.before: Then Naomi arose with her daughters-in-law to return from the country of Moab, because she had heard there that the LORD had attended to his people by giving them food.
verses.after: Naomi set out with her daughters-in-law to return from Moab. While there, she had heard that the LORD had attended to his people and given them food.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then she rose, she and her daughters-in-law, to return from the fields of Moab, for she had heard in the fields of Moab that the LORD had attended to his people and given them bread.

verses.rationale: Keeps both women present and the return motif explicit.
verses.before: She left the place where she had been living, with her two daughters-in-law, and they set out on the road to return to the land of Judah.
verses.after: She left the place where she had been living, with both daughters-in-law beside her. They took the road back to the land of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she set out from the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.

verses.rationale: Retains mother’s household and reciprocal hesed rather than replacing it with general kindness.
verses.before: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you, to your mother’s house. May the LORD show steadfast love to you, just as you have shown steadfast love to the dead and to me.
verses.after: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return, each of you, to your mother’s home. May the LORD show you steadfast love, as you have shown it to the dead and to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each of you to your mother’s house. May the LORD deal with you in steadfast kindness, as you have dealt with the dead and with me.

verses.rationale: Preserves rest as a recurring image rather than explaining it away.
verses.before: May the LORD grant each of you rest in the home of a husband.” Then she kissed them, and they lifted their voices and wept.
verses.after: May the LORD grant each of you rest in the home of a husband.” She kissed them, and they wept aloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD grant that you find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.

verses.rationale: Gives ki its responsive insistence and repeats return.
verses.before: They said to her, “No, we will return with you to your people.”
verses.after: They said to her, “No, we will return with you to your people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they said to her, “No, we will return with you to your people.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the womb question and proposed family relationship explicit.
verses.before: But Naomi said, “Turn back, my daughters. Why would you go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who could become your husbands?
verses.after: But Naomi said, “Return, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who could become your husbands?
verses.tsw_comparator: But Naomi said, “Turn back, my daughters; why will you go with me? Have I yet sons in my womb, that they may become your husbands?

verses.rationale: Maintains the escalating hypothetical across the verse boundary.
verses.before: Turn back, my daughters. Go, because I am too old to have a husband. Even if I said, ‘I still have hope,’ and even if I had a husband tonight and gave birth to sons,
verses.after: Return, my daughters. Go. I am too old to marry again. Even if I thought there was hope for me, even if I had a husband tonight and then bore sons,
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn back, my daughters, go your way, for I am too old to have a husband. Even if I said I have hope, even if I should have a husband this night and also bear sons,

verses.rationale: Chooses comparative mikkem while noting alternative for-your-sake; preserves Naomi’s accusation.
verses.before: would you wait for them until they grew up? Would you remain unmarried for them? No, my daughters. It is far more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.”
verses.after: would you wait until they grew up? Would you keep yourselves from marrying for their sake? No, my daughters. My bitterness is greater than yours, for the LORD’s hand has turned against me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: would you therefore wait until they were grown? Would you therefore refrain from marrying? No, my daughters; for it is exceedingly bitter to me for your sake that the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.”

verses.rationale: Contrasts farewell and clinging without judging Orpah.
verses.before: Then they lifted their voices and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
verses.after: Again they wept aloud. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held tightly to her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they lifted up their voices and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.

verses.rationale: Retains plural gods and sister-in-law relationship.
verses.before: Naomi said, “Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods. Go back after your sister-in-law.”
verses.after: Naomi said, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and her gods. Return with her.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And she said, “See, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods; return after your sister-in-law.”

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated commitments and concrete lodging rather than abstract residence.
verses.before: But Ruth said, “Do not urge me to leave you or to turn back from following you. Where you go, I will go; where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
verses.after: But Ruth said, “Do not press me to leave you and turn back from following you. Wherever you go, I will go. Wherever you spend the night, I will spend the night. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Ruth said, “Do not press me to leave you or to turn back from following you. For where you go, I will go, and where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.

verses.rationale: Renders oath idiom without inventing its unstated curse; notes force of death clause.
verses.before: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD deal with me, ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me.”
verses.after: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD do this to me, and more besides, if anything but death separates you and me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD do thus to me, and more also, if anything but death separates me from you.”

verses.rationale: Names speakers and contextual purpose of ceasing speech.
verses.before: When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.
verses.after: When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she said no more.

verses.rationale: Makes feminine speakers explicit and preserves the town’s astonishment.
verses.before: So the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. When they entered Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred because of them, and the women asked, “Is this Naomi?”
verses.after: The two of them traveled on until they reached Bethlehem. Their arrival stirred the whole town. The women asked, “Can this be Naomi?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. And when they came to Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred because of them; and the women said, “Is this Naomi?”

verses.rationale: Retains names for wordplay note and Naomi’s attribution of bitterness.
verses.before: She said to them, “Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
verses.after: She answered, “Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has made my life deeply bitter.
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to them, “Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.

verses.rationale: Preserves full/empty and forensic anah bi without turning her lament into narrator judgment.
verses.before: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi when the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought calamity upon me?”
verses.after: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi when the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought disaster on me?”
verses.tsw_comparator: I went away full, and the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi, when the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought calamity upon me?”

verses.rationale: Preserves return and foreign identity and ends on the harvest setting.
verses.before: So Naomi returned, and with her Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, who returned from the country of Moab. They came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
verses.after: So Naomi returned from the country of Moab, with Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, beside her. They reached Bethlehem as the barley harvest began.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite her daughter-in-law with her, who returned from the fields of Moab. And they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of barley harvest.

verses.rationale: Preserves hayil as standing and provides family information before naming Boaz.
verses.before: Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side, a man of standing from the clan of Elimelech. His name was Boaz.
verses.after: Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side, a man of standing from Elimelech’s family. His name was Boaz.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Naomi had a relative of her husband, a worthy man of the clan of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.

verses.rationale: Retains gleaning terminology with a concrete object and permission request.
verses.before: Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Let me go to the fields and glean among the heads of grain behind someone in whose eyes I may find favor.” Naomi said to her, “Go, my daughter.”
verses.after: Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Let me go into the fields and glean ears of grain behind someone who will look kindly on me.” Naomi replied, “Go, my daughter.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain after him in whose sight I may find favor.” And she said to her, “Go, my daughter.”

verses.rationale: Preserves chance wording without adding narrator-explicit providence.
verses.before: So Ruth went out and gleaned in the field behind the reapers. As it happened, she came to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.
verses.after: She went out and gleaned in a field behind the harvesters. As it happened, she came to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from Elimelech’s family.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she went and came and gleaned in the field after the reapers. And she happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the clan of Elimelech.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reciprocal blessing as a spoken encounter.
verses.before: Just then Boaz came from Bethlehem. He said to the reapers, “The LORD be with you.” They answered him, “The LORD bless you.”
verses.after: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem. “The LORD be with you,” he said to the harvesters. “The LORD bless you,” they answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem. And he said to the reapers, “The LORD be with you.” And they answered him, “The LORD bless you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves household-affiliation question rather than reducing it to her name.
verses.before: Boaz asked the servant in charge of the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?”
verses.after: Boaz asked the servant supervising the harvesters, “Whose young woman is this?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?”

verses.rationale: Retains the supervisor’s identification by origin and relationship.
verses.before: The servant in charge of the reapers answered, “She is the young Moabite woman who returned with Naomi from the country of Moab.
verses.after: The supervisor answered, “She is the young Moabite woman who returned with Naomi from Moab.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the servant who was set over the reapers answered, “She is the young Moabite woman who returned with Naomi from the country of Moab.

verses.rationale: Uses plausible rest/shelter reading of difficult final clause, flagged in note.
verses.before: She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.’ She came early this morning and has continued until now, with only a short rest.”
verses.after: She asked, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.’ She came this morning and has stayed until now, with only a short rest in the shelter.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the reapers.’ So she came and has continued from early morning until now, except for a short rest.”

verses.rationale: Retains daughter address and the women’s specific company.
verses.before: Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Do not go glean in another field, and do not leave this one. Stay close to my young women.
verses.after: Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Do not go glean in another field or leave this one. Stay close to my young women.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Now listen, my daughter. Do not go to glean in another field or leave this one, but stay close to my young women.

verses.rationale: Keeps gender distinctions and explicit prohibition on touching without softening risk.
verses.before: Keep your eyes on the field they are reaping, and follow after them. I have commanded the young men not to touch you. When you are thirsty, go to the water jars and drink what the young men have drawn.”
verses.after: Watch the field they are harvesting and follow the women. I have ordered the young men not to touch you. When you are thirsty, go to the jars and drink what the young men have drawn.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your eyes be on the field that they are reaping, and go after them. Have I not commanded the young men not to touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink what the young men have drawn.”

verses.rationale: Preserves physical obeisance and notice/foreigner tension.
verses.before: Ruth fell on her face, bowing to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you would take notice of me when I am a foreigner?”
verses.after: She fell facedown, bowing to the ground. “Why have I found favor with you?” she asked. “Why take notice of me, a foreigner?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then she fell on her face, bowing to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, since I am a foreigner?”

verses.rationale: Unfolds report and departure while preserving both parents and unfamiliar people.
verses.before: Boaz answered her, “Everything you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband’s death has been fully told to me—how you left your father and mother and your homeland and came to a people you did not know before.
verses.after: Boaz answered, “I have heard all about what you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband died. You left your father and mother and the land of your birth to come to a people you had never known.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Boaz answered her, “All that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband has been fully told to me, and how you left your father and mother and your native land and came to a people whom you did not know before.

verses.rationale: Retains reward repetition and wings linking to 3:9.
verses.before: May the LORD repay you for what you have done, and may you receive a full reward from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to seek refuge.”
verses.after: May the LORD repay what you have done. May you receive a full reward from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come for refuge.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD repay you for what you have done, and may your reward be full from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to seek refuge.”

verses.rationale: Preserves heart idiom and Ruth’s unequal social position.
verses.before: Ruth said, “May I continue to find favor in your eyes, my lord, because you have comforted me and spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not even one of your servants.”
verses.after: She said, “May I continue to find favor with you, my lord. You have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your servant, though I do not even rank with one of your female servants.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then she said, “I have found favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not even like one of your servants.”

verses.rationale: Retains ancient meal, full eating and surplus for Naomi.
verses.before: At mealtime Boaz said to her, “Come here, eat some of the bread, and dip your piece in the vinegar.” So she sat beside the reapers, and he handed her roasted grain. She ate until she was satisfied and had some left over.
verses.after: At mealtime Boaz told her, “Come here. Have some bread and dip your piece in the sour wine.” She sat beside the harvesters, and he offered her roasted grain. She ate her fill and had some left over.
verses.tsw_comparator: And at mealtime Boaz said to her, “Come here and eat some bread and dip your morsel in the vinegar.” So she sat beside the reapers, and he passed to her roasted grain. And she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.

verses.rationale: Keeps expanded access and shame prohibition distinct from rebuke next verse.
verses.before: When she got up to glean, Boaz instructed his young men, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not shame her.
verses.after: When she got up to glean, Boaz ordered his young men, “Let her glean even among the sheaves. Do not humiliate her.
verses.tsw_comparator: When she rose to glean, Boaz instructed his young men, saying, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not reproach her.

verses.rationale: Makes deliberate provision clear without changing gleaning into a direct gift.
verses.before: In fact, pull out some stalks from the bundles for her and leave them for her to glean. Do not rebuke her.”
verses.after: Pull some stalks out of the bundles for her and leave them for her to glean. Do not rebuke her.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And also pull out some from the bundles for her and leave it for her to glean, and do not rebuke her.”

verses.rationale: Preserves threshing action and approximate ancient measure.
verses.before: Ruth gleaned in the field until evening. Then she beat out what she had gleaned, and it came to about an ephah of barley.
verses.after: Ruth gleaned in the field until evening. Then she beat out the grain she had gathered—about an ephah of barley.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she gleaned in the field until evening. Then she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes gleaned grain from prepared meal leftovers.
verses.before: She carried it into the town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. Ruth also brought out the food she had left after eating her fill and gave it to her.
verses.after: She carried it into town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. Ruth also took out what she had saved after eating her fill and gave it to her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And she took it up and went into the city. Her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. She also brought out and gave her what food she had left over after being satisfied.

verses.rationale: Keeps Naomi’s two questions and notice motif before disclosure of name.
verses.before: Her mother-in-law asked her, “Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the one who took notice of you.” So Ruth told her mother-in-law whom she had worked with. She said, “The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz.”
verses.after: Her mother-in-law asked, “Where did you glean today? Where did you work? A blessing on the man who took notice of you!” Ruth told her who she had worked with. “The man I worked with today is named Boaz.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where did you glean today? And where have you worked? Blessed be the man who took notice of you.” So she told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked and said, “The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz.”

verses.rationale: Main text attaches relative clause to LORD; note preserves possible Boaz referent and family redemption.
verses.before: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the LORD, whose steadfast love has not forsaken the living or the dead.” Naomi also said to her, “The man is a close relative of ours, one of our redeemers.”
verses.after: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not abandoned his steadfast love for the living and the dead.” Then she added, “The man is related to us. He is one of our redeemers.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the LORD, whose steadfast love has not forsaken the living or the dead.” Naomi also said to her, “The man is a close relative of ours, one of our redeemers.”

verses.rationale: Retains Ruth’s masculine wording rather than harmonizing to Boaz’s young women.
verses.before: Ruth the Moabite said, “He also told me, ‘Stay close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.’”
verses.after: Ruth the Moabite continued, “He also told me, ‘Stay close to my young men until they have finished my entire harvest.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Ruth the Moabite said, “He also said to me, ‘Stay close by my young men until they have finished all my harvest.’”

verses.rationale: Retains Naomi’s women and the threat conveyed by paga in context.
verses.before: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that you are not harmed in another field.”
verses.after: Naomi said to Ruth, her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, for you to go out with his young women. In another field someone might assault you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, lest in another field you be harmed.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both harvests and shared household after field work.
verses.before: So Ruth stayed close to the young women of Boaz, gleaning until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest. And she continued living with her mother-in-law.
verses.after: So Ruth stayed close to Boaz’s young women, gleaning until the barley and wheat harvests were over. She continued living with her mother-in-law.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she stayed close to the young women of Boaz, gleaning until the end of the barley harvest and wheat harvest. And she lived with her mother-in-law.

verses.rationale: Connects rest to 1:9 without importing a particular marriage arrangement.
verses.before: Naomi, Ruth’s mother-in-law, said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek rest for you, so that it may go well with you?
verses.after: Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a place of rest for you, where you can fare well?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?

verses.rationale: Explains identity and night’s agricultural activity.
verses.before: Now, isn’t Boaz our relative, whose young women you have been with? Tonight he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
verses.after: Now Boaz, whose young women you have been with, is our relative. Tonight he will be winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, is not Boaz our relative, with whose young women you have been? Behold, he is winnowing barley tonight at the threshing floor.

verses.rationale: Follows qere feminine imperatives; avoids unsupported best clothes or perfume specificity.
verses.before: Wash, anoint yourself, put on your cloak, and go down to the threshing floor. But do not let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
verses.after: Wash, put on oil, get dressed, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wash therefore and anoint yourself, and put on your cloak, and go down to the threshing floor. But do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.

verses.rationale: Retains feet and lying down without inventing a sexual act or denying ambiguity.
verses.before: When he lies down, notice the place where he lies. Then go, uncover his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what to do.”
verses.after: When he lies down, notice where he is lying. Then go in, uncover his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what to do.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when he lies down, observe the place where he lies. Then go and uncover his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what you shall do.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies responding speaker and keeps comprehensive assent.
verses.before: Ruth said to her, “Everything you say, I will do.”
verses.after: Ruth answered, “I will do everything you tell me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And she said to her, “All that you say I will do.”

verses.rationale: Preserves narrated compliance without adding motives.
verses.before: So Ruth went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her.
verses.after: She went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.

verses.rationale: Retains heart and discreet approach without calling him drunk.
verses.before: Boaz ate and drank, and he was in good spirits. Then he went to lie down at the end of the grain pile. Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
verses.after: Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was content. He went to lie down at the far end of the grain heap. Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then she came softly and uncovered his feet and lay down.

verses.rationale: Preserves sudden discovery and unnamed woman in his perspective.
verses.before: At midnight the man was startled and turned over—and there was a woman lying at his feet.
verses.after: In the middle of the night the man startled awake and turned over. There was a woman lying at his feet!
verses.tsw_comparator: At midnight the man was startled and turned over, and behold, a woman lay at his feet.

verses.rationale: Carries garment/wing bridge to refuge in 2:12; does not replace explicit request with marry me.
verses.before: He asked, “Who are you?” She answered, “I am Ruth, your servant. Spread the corner of your garment over your servant, because you are a redeemer.”
verses.after: “Who are you?” he asked. “I am Ruth, your servant,” she replied. “Spread the wing of your garment over your servant, for you are a redeemer.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Who are you?” And she answered, “I am Ruth, your servant. Spread your garment over your servant, for you are a redeemer.”

verses.rationale: Retains hesed comparison and both economic possibilities.
verses.before: Boaz said, “May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have shown greater steadfast love now than at first, because you have not gone after younger men, whether poor or rich.
verses.after: He said, “May the LORD bless you, my daughter. This last act of steadfast love is greater than the first: you have not pursued young men, whether poor or rich.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have made this last kindness greater than the first, in that you have not gone after young men, whether poor or rich.

verses.rationale: Keeps hayil link to Boaz and civic gate image.
verses.before: Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do everything you ask, because everyone in town knows that you are a woman of standing.
verses.after: Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do everything you ask. Everyone at the gate of my town knows that you are a woman of standing.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, my daughter, do not fear. I will do for you all that you ask, for all my fellow townsmen know that you are a worthy woman.

verses.rationale: Follows qere omission of im and preserves priority by kinship.
verses.before: It is true that I am a redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.
verses.after: It is true that I am a redeemer, but there is another redeemer more closely related than I am.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now it is true that I am a redeemer. Yet there is a redeemer nearer than I.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional sequence, repeated redemption and oath.
verses.before: Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he will redeem you, good—let him do it. But if he is not willing to redeem you, then as the LORD lives, I will redeem you. Lie down until morning.”
verses.after: Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he will redeem you, good—let him do it. But if he does not want to redeem you, then, as the LORD lives, I will. Lie down until morning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Remain tonight, and in the morning, if he will redeem you, good; let him do it. But if he is not willing to redeem you, then as the LORD lives, I will redeem you. Lie down until the morning.”

verses.rationale: Retains limited dawn visibility and Boaz’s concern without attributing guilt.
verses.before: So Ruth lay at his feet until morning, but she got up before one person could recognize another. Boaz said, “It must not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”
verses.after: She lay at his feet until morning, then got up before one person could recognize another. Boaz said, “No one must know that a woman came to the threshing floor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So she lay at his feet until the morning, but arose before one could recognize another. And he said, “Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”

verses.rationale: Preserves unspecified units and masculine he went in pinned Hebrew.
verses.before: Then he said, “Bring me the cloak you are wearing and hold it out.” She held it out, and he measured six measures of barley and placed it on her. Then he went into the town.
verses.after: He said, “Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” She held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and lifted the load onto her. Then he went into town.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “Bring the cloak you are wearing and hold it out.” So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and laid it on her. Then he went into the city.

verses.rationale: Uses contextual status inquiry; notes literal who are you echo of 3:9.
verses.before: When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, “How did it go, my daughter?” Ruth told her everything the man had done for her.
verses.after: When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, “How did it go, my daughter?” Ruth told her everything the man had done for her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when she came to her mother-in-law, she said, “How did it go, my daughter?” Then she told her all that the man had done for her,

verses.rationale: Keeps six unspecified measures and empty link to 1:21.
verses.before: She said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, because he told me, ‘You must not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
verses.after: She added, “He gave me these six measures of barley. He told me, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “These six measures of barley he gave to me, for he said to me, ‘You must not go back empty-handed to your mother-in-law.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves rest contrast and urgency of today.
verses.before: Naomi said, “Wait, my daughter, until you learn how the matter turns out. The man will not rest until he settles the matter today.”
verses.after: Naomi said, “Stay here, my daughter, until you know how this turns out. The man will not rest until he has settled the matter today.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She replied, “Wait, my daughter, until you learn how the matter turns out, for the man will not rest but will settle the matter today.”

verses.rationale: Retains deliberately withheld name with gate setting.
verses.before: Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down there. Just then, the redeemer Boaz had spoken about came by. Boaz said, “Come over here, so-and-so, and sit down.” So the man came over and sat down.
verses.after: Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down. Just then the redeemer he had spoken of passed by. “Come over and sit here, so-and-so,” Boaz called. The man came over and sat down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Boaz had gone up to the gate and sat down there. And behold, the redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken passed by. So Boaz said, “Turn aside, friend. Sit down here.” And he turned aside and sat down.

verses.rationale: Preserves ten witnesses and repeated seating.
verses.before: Boaz gathered ten of the town elders and said, “Sit down here.” So they sat down.
verses.after: Boaz gathered ten of the town’s elders. “Sit here,” he said, and they sat down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he took ten men of the elders of the city and said, “Sit down here.” So they sat down.

verses.rationale: Uses transaction-in-progress understanding of makherah; note retains has sold possibility.
verses.before: Then Boaz said to the redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the country of Moab, is selling the parcel of land that belonged to our relative Elimelech.
verses.after: He told the redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our relative Elimelech.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to the redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the country of Moab, is selling the parcel of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

verses.rationale: Retains Hebrew third-person negative condition impersonally and clear priority of rights.
verses.before: I thought I should inform you and say, ‘Buy it in the presence of those sitting here and in the presence of the elders of my people.’ If you will redeem it, redeem it. But if you will not, tell me so I will know, because no one has the right to redeem it before you, and I come after you.” The man said, “I will redeem it.”
verses.after: I thought I should bring it to your attention: buy it here before those seated with us and the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, do so. If it is not to be redeemed, tell me so I will know. You have the first right to redeem it, and I come after you.” “I will redeem it,” the man said.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I thought I would tell you of it and say, ‘Buy it in the presence of those sitting here and in the presence of the elders of my people.’ If you will redeem it, redeem it. But if you will not, tell me, that I may know, for there is no one besides you to redeem it, and I come after you.” And he said, “I will redeem it.”

verses.rationale: Follows qere you acquire with contextual acquisition of Ruth; note records ketiv I acquire and difficult preposition.
verses.before: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the field from Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the widow of the dead man, in order to preserve the dead man’s name with his inheritance.”
verses.after: Then Boaz said, “On the day you acquire the field from Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the dead man’s widow, to preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Boaz said, “The day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the widow of the dead, in order to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.”

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated refusal and stated inheritance concern without inventing economic mechanics.
verses.before: The redeemer said, “I cannot redeem it for myself, because I might damage my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption for yourself, because I cannot redeem it.”
verses.after: The redeemer replied, “I cannot redeem it for myself without jeopardizing my own inheritance. Take over my right of redemption. I cannot redeem it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the redeemer said, “I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I impair my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption for yourself, for I cannot redeem it.”

verses.rationale: Keeps explanatory narrator aside distinct from Deuteronomic humiliation rite.
verses.before: In former times in Israel, this was the custom concerning redemption and exchange: to confirm a matter, one man removed his sandal and gave it to the other. This was how an agreement was formally confirmed in Israel.
verses.after: In earlier times in Israel, this was the practice for confirming a redemption or an exchange: a man took off his sandal and gave it to the other party. This served as proof of the transaction in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now this was the custom in former times in Israel concerning redemption and exchange: to confirm a matter, one man removed his sandal and gave it to another. And this was the manner of attestation in Israel.

verses.rationale: Links refusal and sandal action with acquisition vocabulary.
verses.before: So the redeemer said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself,” and he removed his sandal.
verses.after: So the redeemer said to Boaz, “Acquire it for yourself,” and took off his sandal.
verses.tsw_comparator: So when the redeemer said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself,” he removed his sandal.

verses.rationale: Retains all three men and public witness declaration.
verses.before: Then Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I have acquired from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech and everything that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon.
verses.after: Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “Today you are witnesses that I have acquired from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses this day that I have bought from the hand of Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech and all that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon.

verses.rationale: Retains acquisition language and name preservation without sanitizing ancient legal terms.
verses.before: I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, in order to preserve the dead man’s name with his inheritance, so that his name will not be cut off from among his relatives or from the gate of his hometown. You are witnesses today.”
verses.after: I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, to preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance. His name must not disappear from among his relatives or from the gate of his hometown. Today you are witnesses.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Also Ruth the Moabite, the widow of Mahlon, I have acquired as my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead may not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his native place. You are witnesses this day.”

verses.rationale: Keeps house-building image and both matriarchs before place/name blessing.
verses.before: All the people at the gate and the elders said, “We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is coming into your house like Rachel and Leah, who together built the house of Israel. May you prosper in Ephrathah and make a name for yourself in Bethlehem.
verses.after: All the people at the gate and the elders replied, “We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman entering your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built the house of Israel. May you prosper in Ephrathah and make a name in Bethlehem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the people who were at the gate and the elders said, “We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is coming into your house like Rachel and Leah, who together built the house of Israel. May you prosper in Ephrathah and be renowned in Bethlehem.

verses.rationale: Preserves Tamar’s agency and precise genealogy in blessing.
verses.before: And may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman.”
verses.after: Through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman, may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, because of the offspring that the LORD will give you by this young woman.”

verses.rationale: Keeps marriage, intercourse and conception as separate source actions.
verses.before: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He slept with her, and the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son.
verses.after: Boaz took Ruth as his wife and slept with her. The LORD enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. And he went in to her, and the LORD gave her conception, and she bore a son.

verses.rationale: Keeps child-associated redeemer language and ambiguity of his name without inserting Boaz.
verses.before: Then the women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you today without a redeemer. May his name become renowned in Israel.
verses.after: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you without a redeemer today! May his name be renowned in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you this day without a redeemer. And may his name be renowned in Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains restoration, seven sons and explicit Ruth love.
verses.before: He will restore your life and sustain you in your old age, because your daughter-in-law who loves you has given birth to him—she who is better to you than seven sons.”
verses.after: He will restore your life and sustain you in old age. Your daughter-in-law, who loves you, has borne him—she who is better to you than seven sons.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall be to you a restorer of life and a sustainer of your old age, for your daughter-in-law who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has borne him.”

verses.rationale: Renders heq and omeneth concretely without asserting nursing or formal adoption.
verses.before: Naomi took the child, held him close, and cared for him.
verses.after: Naomi took the child into her lap and became his caregiver.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Naomi took the child and laid him on her lap and became his nurse.

verses.rationale: Retains women’s naming and social birth announcement without changing biological maternity.
verses.before: The neighborhood women gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi.” They named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.
verses.after: The neighboring women gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi!” They named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the women of the neighborhood gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi.” And they called his name Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.

verses.rationale: Keeps toledoth formula connecting earlier family records.
verses.before: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron,
verses.after: These are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron,
verses.tsw_comparator: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron,

verses.rationale: Preserves both links in the line without adding generations.
verses.before: Hezron fathered Ram, Ram fathered Amminadab,
verses.after: Hezron fathered Ram, Ram fathered Amminadab,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hezron fathered Ram, Ram fathered Amminadab,

verses.rationale: Retains source Salmah form distinct from Salmon in next verse, explained in note.
verses.before: Amminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmon,
verses.after: Amminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Amminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmon,

verses.rationale: Preserves source Salmon form and repeated fathering.
verses.before: Salmon fathered Boaz, Boaz fathered Obed,
verses.after: Salmon fathered Boaz, Boaz fathered Obed,
verses.tsw_comparator: Salmon fathered Boaz, Boaz fathered Obed,

verses.rationale: Ends genealogy and book with David as source does.
verses.before: Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.
verses.after: Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

comparative_references.scope: All 85 TSW verses read after drafting independently from every pinned Hebrew verse and its source notes.
